verdict.rationale: Supabase's MCP server and BYO-MCP docs describe scoped tool access tied to RLS/service-role permissions (supabase-docs-1, supabase-docs-2, supabase-docs-45), and community reporting confirms Supabase added a read-only-by-default mode plus anti-injection safeguards for the MCP server (supabase-comm-2). However, a concrete hands-on exploit report shows an attacker was able to use prompt injection via the MCP server to have an agent bypass RLS through service_role access and exfiltrate a sensitive table (supabase-comm-1), directly contradicting the 'safely delegate' framing even after mitigations were applied. missing for 10: first-party documentation of a formal read-only vs destructive tool distinction/permission schema, and independent confirmation that the exploit is now fully closed.
